CHN.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Send Liu He into this week's Washington round to seek a narrow truce that stops the 15 October hike of List 3 from 25% to 30% and keeps List 4B off the 15 December calendar, without signing structural legal changes or a large new purchase quota that is not matched by U.S. tariff relief. Hold the existing retaliatory schedule and the unused unreliable-entity list in reserve; do not fire either this week. Use already-signaled farm exemptions and ASF-driven pork/soy demand as bargaining chips, not as unilateral concessions.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is high but not existential. Since May the United States has raised List 3 to 25%, put Huawei and dozens of affiliates on the Entity List (licenses remain presumption-of-denial; TGL only through 18 November), designated China a currency manipulator after CNY broke 7, and put 15% List 4A on ~$110–125B of our exports with List 4B still set for 15 December (timeline 2019-05-10 through 2019-09-01; web_search on Entity List expansion). That maps to the CHN +0.5 anchor: major export sectors hit, FX pressure, firm-level Huawei targeting. Country-health confirms the bite: merchandise exports down about 1.4% over the window, industrial production still expanding but only ~4.7% YoY after August's multi-year low, CPI rising (index 110.8) as pork shortages bite, and USD/CNY near 7.13. Reserves are stable near $3.12T and IP has not collapsed, so this is not +1.0. Action should not escalate: the August $75B retaliation produced Trump's 'leave China' order and a 10%→15% List 4 hike, and another shot now would make the 15 October 25%→30% step and December consumer-electronics tariffs more likely. Nor is a purchase-heavy concession appropriate before the U.S. tables a matching tariff pause — talks reopen this week with expectations already toned down (Liu not styled as Xi's special envoy; possible early departure). Negotiate is therefore the stance: lock in a pause, trade farm buying we need anyway for ASF, and keep structural red lines closed.
key_factors: Oct 15 List-3 hike 25% to 30% still scheduled; List 4A already live; List 4B still set for Dec 15
Huawei remains on Entity List with 46 more affiliates added in August; TGL only through 18 Nov
CNY broke 7 in August; Treasury manipulator designation; spot still ~7.13
China IP/export slowdown and pork-driven CPI rise raise domestic-stability cost of further escalation
Goodwill already extended (16-category exemptions; soy/pork additional-tariff exclusions); U.S. only delayed the hike two weeks
13th-round Washington talks this week with low expectations and unresolved May collapse over sovereignty/enforcement

sources_cited.excerpt: US Commerce Department adds Huawei and affiliates to the Entity List. US firms generally barred from selling to Huawei without a license.
After the Shanghai round, Trump announces 10% tariffs on the remaining ~$300B of Chinese goods (List 4), effective Sept 1.
After CNY breaks 7 per USD, US Treasury designates China a currency manipulator (first such designation since 1994).

China announces retaliation on ~$75B of US goods... Trump orders US companies to immediately start looking for an alternative to China and directs a 5-point increase on the planned List 4 rate (to 15%).
List 4A takes effect at 15% (~$110–125B of Chinese imports). China's first tranche of the ~$75B retaliation also takes effect.
China announces first tariff-exemption list for some US products (16 categories; industrial inputs / chemicals / related — not a broad farm rollback).
Chinese state media reports soybeans, pork, and some other farm goods will be excluded from additional retaliatory tariffs (goodwill signal ahead of talks).
China merchandise exports latest 207.7B USD, change -1.36% over the 180-day window.
China industrial production index 104.7 (latest), still positive YoY but down 0.3 pts in-window after a weak August.
CNY per USD 7.1316 on 2019-10-09, +6.3% depreciation over the window after breaking 7 in early August.
China CPI index 110.8 latest, +3.0 pts / +2.8% in-window as food/pork pressure builds.
China reserves ex-gold ~$3.125T, essentially flat (+0.15%), so no reserve-crisis signal.
13th-round talks this week; Liu He not carrying 'special envoy' title; source says delegation may cut stay short; U.S. still scheduled to raise tariffs on $250B from 25% to 30%.
Trump delayed the 25% to 30% hike on $250B from Oct 1 to Oct 15 as a 'gesture of good will' at Liu He's request around the PRC 70th anniversary — delay only, not cancellation.
August industrial production +4.4% YoY, weakest in 17+ years; retail sales also slowed — downside risk cited as a reason China softened its trade stance.
BIS added 46 additional Huawei affiliates to the Entity List in August with presumption of denial, tightening the May 16 listing rather than easing it.
